findings.summary: When a screen's last block is a form (a checkout under the cart), the closing-statement rule rewrites its plain heading into the 96px two-tone display statement over the dot field ('All set? Fill this in.', 'Almost yours. Where to?'). The form drops below a large headline and the cart page goes from a side-by-side layout to a stacked one. The reference uses its statement only to close a page over its action pills, never above a form (pipeline/linear-study/reference/screenshots/p1-desktop-light.png). The rule is followed, so this is the spec's reading of 'closing block', not an agent slip.
findings.promptFix: Only a block that ends a page with one final action for the reader (subscribe, sign up, contact) is a page close. A form that is the main content of its screen, such as a checkout or a settings form, keeps its plain section heading and is never rewritten into the display statement.

findings.summary: The pinned status column of a table draws a vertical hairline along its left edge on desktop (dashboard projects table, billing invoices table). It reads as a stray divider in an otherwise horizontal-rule table. The reference's tables have no vertical rules.
Store header: the full-width header border sits 1px above the page opener's own rule, so two hairlines show under the header on the shop page (measured double-rule, real but small).
Blog plate captions carry a count ('585 WORDS', '3 PARTS') that is real but tells the posts apart weakly. The store's captions ('18 OZ', 'BRASS') carry more. Carried over from the earlier round.

On the newsletter form, the input and its button end 2px apart in the one sample that puts them on one row (measured uneven-row). It is visible at 2x as the button sitting slightly lower than the field.

notes: Scope: the confirm step, three samples of blog, commerce, dashboard and settings (20261019-035003, -070800-s1, -070800-s2) plus one sample each of the docs and landing holdouts. I looked at the desktop and mobile home and route screenshots, the dark pages I spot-checked, the state captures (checkout errors, newsletter error, plan dialog, signup error, keyboard focus), drawing crops and the landing motion frames. Reference: p1-desktop-light.png. All gates passed (eval-2.md). The page close is the update goal; I checked it on every sample.

Update goal (iterations.md, 1.2.0-rc.4): reached. Every blog sample ends on a two-sentence, two-tone statement over the dot field ('Get new notes. Nothing else.', 'Read along. By email.', 'Get new posts. By email.') with the mono label above it. The landing holdout does the same on home, pricing and customers ('Stop chasing. Start meeting.'). At 390px it breaks only between the two sentences (blog s2 mobile, landing mobile). This matches the reference close. The rc.3 major is fixed in all three samples, and no earlier blocker or major came back. Settings blocks still end at the controls column's right edge, billing plans are ranked 1-2-3, and the empty-cart blueprint stack and error banner placement hold.
Regressions vs published 1.1.0: none found. The close is the one visible change, and it is closer to the reference.

Holdouts: no blocker. Docs and landing carry the system: hairline grids, plate captions, split openers, stage with the product screen, mono labels, inverse pill CTAs. Docs has no closing block, which is correct for its structure.

Measured defect, blog / double-rule (desktop 'featured-post' plate and mobile tag chips): false alarm. The plate's own border meets the opener's rule by design, and the chips sit on the card edge. I see no doubled line in the screenshots.
Measured defect, blog / uneven-row (newsletter input and button, 2px): real but tiny, listed as a minor. In the other two samples the form is stacked, so the defect is not there.

Measured defect, commerce / repeated-drawing (all samples): false alarm. There are eleven products and eight plate kinds, so a kind repeats only after the eighth, each time with a different caption (FIG 05 '240 GSM' vs FIG 10 'BRASS'). No kind repeats in a row or column.
Measured defect, commerce s1 / double-rule header: real, listed as a minor.

Measured defects, landing: the mobile clipped-text on the hero calendar (day and hour labels past div.stage-window) is a false alarm. The window deliberately crops a wide product screen at 390px, the way the reference crops its product shot, and the labels are decoration inside a cropped preview. uneven-row on pw-col/pw-slot is a false alarm: the cells are calendar grid cells of different heights by design. Pricing and customers double-rule (table row rules against opener lines, 1px) are not visible as doubled lines in pricing-desktop-light.png or customers-desktop-light.png. customers repeated-drawing: false alarm, eight different drawings with distinct captions. The docs changelog inline-code 'double-rule' is a false alarm, since code chips sit on a text line.
Capture artifact, not penalized: the dialog backdrop is cut at y=900 in the settings plan-dialog state, as in earlier rounds.
Known and not re-raised: the blueprints use clean single outlines, not the reference's ribbed tiers. The loop motion (bp-dash, 1000ms linear) is subtle but present in the motion frames.
Scores are descriptive. Reference fidelity 4. Cross-app consistency 4. Hierarchy 4. Spacing 4. Component states 4. Polish 4. Signature 4.
Verdict basis: no blocker and no major, so the candidate passes the confirm step.
